slides.main: Low DAO result? It proves nothing about histamine intolerance.
slides.sub: Why the test says so little, and what to do instead.

slides.main: Whether histamine intolerance really occurs is unclear, and there is no reliable test.
slides.sub: Several studies found similar blood DAO levels in people with symptoms and in healthy people.

slides.main: Flushing, itching, nausea, diarrhoea and tummy pain are often described.
slides.sub: None of these symptoms is unique to histamine, so get other causes checked first.

slides.main: Histamine food lists contradict each other.
slides.sub: Ten low histamine diets agreed on only one group: fermented foods.

slides.main: Rule out other causes, then eat less histamine for 10 to 14 days.
slides.sub: Then bring suspected foods back, ideally with a dietitian. The approach rests on experience; controlled studies are missing.

slides.main: Get medical help if you have:
items: Swollen lips, tongue or throat after eating: emergency
Breathless or faint after eating: call emergency number
Blood in your stool or black stools
